questions.question:
Six letters, G, H, I, J, K and L are written on different faces of a dice. Three positions of this dice are shown here. Find the letter on the face opposite L.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fcbe1b2f015d19f3266d53b52916b2412259b8200982769a96111d8d1c9a67b9.png]
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

From the given three different dices the adjacent sides are as shown below :

As L is common on both the dices II and III, it is clear that H, K, J, and G are adjacent to it, and the remaining i.e. I will be opposite to it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/711507ac2ff9664a4a5515cc3b6f64d93d89b25cb1dd399d39a126db6ff75b16.png] 

Opposite pairs:

H → G

K → J

L → I

So, the opposite side of "L" will be side "I".

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)

(50, 63), (101, 120)
questions.solution:
The logic follows here:

1st number = (Any number)² + 1

2nd number = (Any number + 1)² - 1

Given:

(50, 63)

1st number = (7)2 + 1 = 49 + 1 = 50

2nd number = (7 + 1)2 - 1 = 82 - 1 = 64 - 1 = 63

And,

(101, 120) 

1st number = (10)2 + 1 = 100 + 1 = 101

2nd number = (10 + 1)2 - 1 = 112 - 1 = 121 - 1 = 120

Similarly, **Option (2): (145, 168)**

**1st number = (12)2 + 1 = 144 + 1 = 145**

**2nd number = (12 + 1)2 - 1 = 132 - 1 = 169 - 1 = 168**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option (2)".**

questions.question:
Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series.

S _ _ A D _ Q W _ D _ Q W A _ S Q _ _ D
questions.solution:
Given series: S _ _ A D _ Q W _ D _ Q W A _ S Q _ _ D

Option 1) QWSASAWD → S __Q__ __W__ A D __S__ Q W __A__ D __S__ Q W A __A__ S Q __W__ __D__ D → (It doesn't follow any pattern)

Option 2) QWSASDWA → S __**Q**__ __**W**__ A D __**S**__ Q W __**A**__ D __**S**__ Q W A __**D**__ S Q __**W**__ __**A**__ D → (It follows the pattern of: SQWAD - SQWAD - SQWAD - SQWAD)

Option 3) QWSAADWA → S __Q__ __W__ A D __S__ Q W __A__ D __A__ Q W A __D__ S Q __W__ __A__ D → (It doesn't follow any pattern)

Option 4) QWSASDQA → S __Q__ __W__ A D __S__ Q W __A__ D __S__ Q W A __D__ S Q __Q__ __A__ D → (It doesn't follow any pattern)

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All chips are snacks.

Some fried foods are chips.

**Conclusions:**

I. All fried foods are snacks.

II. Some snacks are fried foods.

III. No fried food is snack.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
Either conclusion I or III follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/81bd5c17b0bc483b56030b120904c099f92238e44f6b9e052e61f217c0de5f34.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All fried foods are snacks → Does not follow (As all chips are snacks and some fried foods are chips. As some part of fried foods is common with chips which whole comes in snacks, therefore it is possible but not definite.)

II. Some snacks are fried foods → Follow (As all chips are snacks and some fried foods are chips. As some part of fried foods is common with chips which whole comes in snacks, therefore it is true.)

III. No fried food is snack → Does not follow (As all chips are snacks and some fried foods are chips. As some part of fried foods is common with chips which whole comes in snacks, therefore it is false.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion II follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".
